memory_update.text: LEU is the highest-purity US-listed enrichment/HALEU candidate for this node; key survival test is funded commercial-scale capacity, not just licensing or DOE eligibility.

XE is a newly public 2026 fuel-fabrication discovery candidate; its TRISO-X NRC Part 70 HALEU fuel-fabrication license makes it more directly relevant to the node than a generic SMR screen would show.
LTBR should remain speculative_shadow until irradiation testing, pilot-fabrication funding, licensing path, and customer adoption are materially de-risked.

Cameco/CCJ is a major US-listed conversion reference via Port Hope and Westinghouse exposure, but because it is large-cap and high-attention in uranium, later layers should compare it separately against purer US enrichment/fabrication names.

DOE HALEU deconversion awardees also include Framatome, GE Vernova, Orano, Westinghouse, BWXT, and Centrus; several are private, foreign/state-owned, or diversified, so public-market exposure may be indirect.

node: Nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks: conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and fuel fabrication
summary: Layer 1B expansion finds a narrow US-listed universe for the downstream nuclear fuel-cycle bottleneck. The cleanest direct exposure remains Centrus Energy for US HALEU enrichment, but the public universe broadened in 2026 with X-energy/XE as a newly public reactor-and-fuel platform whose TRISO-X subsidiary has an NRC Part 70 HALEU fuel-fabrication license. BWX Technologies is a larger reference/second-order fuel-cycle supplier via DOE HALEU deconversion and HALEU feedstock work, while Lightbridge is a small-cap speculative shadow candidate tied to advanced HALEU-based fuel design and future pilot fabrication rather than current commercial capacity. Key diligence should separate licensed capacity, DOE eligibility, actual funded task orders, construction status, customer/offtake, and whether revenue is material versus narrative-only.
